scene_type.description: Bickham Scene & Sequel classification. Action scenes are disaster-driven (goal → conflict → disaster); sequel scenes are decision-driven (reaction → dilemma → decision). Optional — not every scene card needs this labelled, but workshop plan-level scene cards carry it through from Step 8.

scene_role.description: Narrative function of this scene within its chapter. 'decision_and_plant' = composite role: the scene resolves the chapter's decision beat AND plants a hook/callback for later chapters, common in dense mid-book scenes that cannot afford a dedicated plant scene.

dialogue_expectation.description: Expected dialogue mode for this scene. Drives drafter/revision behavior. `dialogue_led` = 40-55% dialogue target, back-and-forth exchange carries the scene. `balanced` = no hard floor, dialogue and interiority share weight. `interior` = POV-isolation scene, interior monologue and observation dominate even if additional characters are physically present. When omitted, derive() in src/quality/dialogue_expectation.py infers a safe default from scene_type/conflict_type/characters_present. Explicit override is the escape hatch for scenes where a second character is background (e.g. sparring partner in a sequel scene).

dialogue_density_target.description: Optional explicit dialogue-density target consumed by ProseStylist and RhythmValidator. `high` = 55%+ dialogue-bearing paragraphs (Zahn baseline ~67%); `medium` = 35-55%; `low` = <35% (POV-isolation, atmospheric, contemplative scenes). When omitted, the drafter and validator derive a default from `dialogue_expectation` and `characters_present`: any scene with 2+ characters present and `dialogue_expectation` != `interior` defaults to `high`. The RhythmValidator's `dialogue_starved` check only fires when the resolved target is `high` or `medium`.

interiority_budget.description: Optional interiority-rationing contract consumed by ProseStylist. Caps the total word count and paragraph count of interior-monologue / character-reflection prose in this scene so the drafter cannot accrete pages of 'he did not name the feeling' style rumination. Default when omitted: derive from `dialogue_expectation` (`dialogue_led` → 150 words / 2 paragraphs; `balanced` → 250 / 3; `interior` → 600 / 6).

max_words.description: Total interior-monologue word budget across the scene. The drafter should treat this as a hard ceiling, not a target. A scene with multiple short reflection beats is better than one long inner-monologue paragraph.

max_paragraphs.description: Total interior-monologue paragraph budget. Caps the number of distinct unbroken interior beats. Reflection beats longer than this count must be broken with dialogue, action, or environmental interruption.

rationale.description: Optional note explaining why this scene gets the budget it does. Useful when a scene deviates from the default derived from dialogue_expectation (e.g. an interior scene budgeted tight, or a dialogue-led scene granted extra reflection because it's a major emotional pivot).

turning_point_detail.description: Decomposed turning-point planning. When present, the brief assembler uses these three fields directly; when absent, the assembler falls back to the legacy string `turning_point`. Authors planning a new scene should populate this; legacy cards can omit it until migrated. Load-bearing for post-PlotArchitect deterministic brief assembly.

shift.description: How scene dynamics change after the trigger.

cost.description: What the turn costs the POV character — emotional, relational, or strategic.

emotional_arc.description: Decomposed emotional trajectory across the scene. When present, the brief assembler uses these three fields directly; when absent, the assembler falls back to the legacy string `emotional_trajectory`. Authors planning a new scene should populate this; legacy cards can omit it until migrated.

start.description: Starting emotional state — be specific, not a generic label.

shift.description: The pivot — what changes and why.

opening_mode.description: How the scene opens. Drives the drafter's first-paragraph choices. Optional: when absent, the drafter picks an opening appropriate to the scene_role / structural_phase.

key_beats.description: 3-5 specific story beats the scene must execute, in order. Populated during planning (was PlotArchitect runtime output pre-retirement). When present, the brief assembler passes these directly to the drafter as labeled beat sections; when absent, the assembler produces a partial brief and emits a warn event so the operator sees the planning gap.

beat_description.description: What happens observably. One sentence, clear verbs.

state_change.description: What shifts in the external situation or relationship as a result of the beat.

pov_reaction.description: Behavioral / sensory shape of the POV character's internal response — NOT the sentence the drafter should write. Faithful models copy lyrical phrasings verbatim, collapsing voice variety; describe the shape (sensation, impulse, tension, decision-direction) instead.

anti_patterns.description: Structural / compositional moves the drafter must avoid in this scene (e.g., 'do not open with a flashback', 'avoid exposition dump', 'no mission-debrief sentences'). Voice-register anti-patterns belong in `scene_voice_permissions.anti_patterns` — the brief assembler merges both sources into the drafter's anti_patterns surface.

stakes.description: What is at risk in this scene across three dimensions.

personal.description: What the POV character personally stands to lose or gain.

interpersonal.description: What is at risk in relationships between characters.

external.description: What is at risk in the wider story world.

promises_progressed.description: Promise IDs this scene advances without paying off. Used by the Slice 3 promise ledger to record progression beats; each entry appends one row to promise.progression_log at save time with source='scene_card'. Optional.

relationship_deltas.description: Slice 5: per-scene relationship shifts the scene author declares. Each delta is capped at ±0.5 on every axis to prevent runaway swings; authors decompose larger changes across multiple scenes. Used by src/memory/sociogram.py to update edge state at scene-save time.

action_beats.description: 2-4 specific physical actions or state changes that must occur in this scene (e.g., 'draws lightsaber', 'ship enters hyperspace', 'confronts the senator'). Ensures sufficient interest density.

scene_voice_permissions.description: Additive, franchise-agnostic scene-level voice contract. When present, runtime helpers prefer these fields and fall back to legacy top-level voice fields (primary_anchor, supporting_anchor, stover_permitted) only when the corresponding generic keys are absent.

notes.description: Scene-specific voice guidance that should be elevated into the drafter and canon-expert prompt surfaces.

anti_patterns.description: Scene-specific prose or framing moves that are disallowed.

pov_arc_phase.description: Optional local override or mirror of the POV arc phase for voice-register guidance.

anchor_profile.description: Optional prose-anchor guidance for this scene.

authorized_modes.description: Scene-level style permissions granted for this scene. The current canonical mode is heightened_interiority; legacy stover_permitted:true normalizes to this mode at runtime.

prohibited_modes.description: Scene-level style permissions explicitly disallowed for this scene. Legacy stover_permitted:false normalizes to prohibited_modes=[heightened_interiority] at runtime.

revelations.description: revelation_ids (or legacy info_ids) from the concept seed's revelation_schedule

pov_arc_phase.description: POV character's current Weiland arc phase

arc_phase_transition.description: If this scene triggers a phase change, the new phase

depends_on.description: Scene IDs (format chNN_scMM) that this scene directly depends on. Used by SuccessorClassifier (src/pipeline/successor_classifier.py) to classify this scene as an immediate-sequel soft-halt when any listed predecessor is isolated by the state firewall. Authors set this manually; no auto-inference in v1. Optional — missing means classifier falls through to heuristic rules.
